root_cause.text: The Cadence QSPI driver's `cqspi_remove()` path disabled the controller registers before ensuring the device was runtime-resumed, so unbind could perform a register access while the controller clock/power was already gated.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `cqspi_controller_enable(cqspi, 0)` behind `pm_runtime_get_sync(&pdev->dev)` and only executes it when `ret >= 0`, with the commit message explicitly stating this is to “avoid an unclocked register access” during driver unbind.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch moves `cqspi_controller_enable(cqspi, 0)` behind `pm_runtime_get_sync(&pdev->dev)` and only executes it when `ret >= 0`, with the commit message explicitly stating this is to “avoid an unclocked register access” during driver unbind.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix cqspi removal so controller shutdown only occurs after a successful runtime PM resume.
intent_record.what: The unconditional call to `cqspi_controller_enable(cqspi, 0);` was removed from `cqspi_remove()`, and that disable call was moved inside the `if (ret >= 0)` block so it now executes only when `pm_runtime_get_sync(&pdev->dev)` succeeds, together with `clk_bulk_disable_unprepare(CLK_QSPI_NUM, cqspi->clks);`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the controller is now only disabled after the device has been successfully resumed through runtime PM, avoiding an attempt to touch hardware in an unsupported or failed power state. This makes teardown safer by ensuring the clock and controller shutdown sequence only runs when the device is accessible.

grouping_result.intent: Fix cqspi removal so controller shutdown only occurs after a successful runtime PM resume.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it fixes cqspi removal by ensuring the controller is runtime-resumed before shutdown/register access, preventing accesses while clocks/power are gated.

candidates.rationale: This disables the controller registers before the driver has ensured the device is runtime-resumed. If runtime PM has already gated clocks/power, this register access can occur while the hardware is inaccessible.

This is the runtime-resume step that should have happened before any controller register shutdown. Its placement after cqspi_controller_enable(0) reflects the faulty ordering that allowed unsafe register access first.

This gates the controller clock, and if done before the register-disable operation or without a successful resume, subsequent register access in remove can fault. It is part of the unsafe shutdown sequence described by the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This register-disable operation was executed before the driver first ensured the device was runtime-resumed, so it could touch controller registers after clocks/power had already been gated.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is present in the original remove path, but this commit already fixes it by changing the order in `cqspi_remove()`. The snippet shows `spi_unregister_controller(cqspi->host);` followed by `cqspi_controller_enable(cqspi, 0);` and only later the runtime-PM resume/clock disable sequence: `if (!(ddata && (ddata->quirks & CQSPI_DISABLE_RUNTIME_PM))) if (pm_runtime_get_sync(&pdev->dev) >= 0) clk_disable(cqspi->clk);`. This means the controller is disabled after unbinding as part of the corrected teardown order, not before the runtime-resume/clock handling. The diff also explicitly says: `Replicate these changes in the remove path as well.` Therefore the fix is already present and the vulnerable ordering is no longer present in this commit.
